_: The picture-book looks a teacher can choose for a storybook, and the instruction FLUX.2 Klein 4B gets for each page: {style} is one of the styles below, {keep} is what the class's checking model listed as the page's must-keep contents (prompts/picture-keep.txt). Seven styles were tried on the test class's drawings and the operator kept all seven: watercolour, gouache, cut paper and clay change the look clearly; coloured pencil stays close to a crayon drawing, and storybook painting and ink-and-wash change it a little (docs/measured/storybook-styles.md). The order is the order the teacher sees them in; studio/page/src/29l-book-look.js names the same keys.

styles.watercolour: a loose, wet watercolour painting with soft bleeding edges, visible washes and white paper showing through
styles.gouache: a bold, flat gouache painting with crisp shapes and rich saturated colours, like a modern printed picture book
styles.paper: a cut-paper collage of hand-painted tissue papers, with visible torn and cut paper edges and layered textures
styles.clay: a scene of handmade clay and plasticine models, photographed as a miniature set with soft studio light
styles.pencil: a rich coloured-pencil and wax-crayon drawing with clean, confident outlines and warm, even colour
styles.storybook: a soft painterly storybook illustration with gentle light and shadow, rounded forms and a warm glow
styles.ink: a Chinese ink-and-wash painting with expressive black brush lines and light, transparent colour washes on rice paper
